subject.title: chore(deps): bump the production-minor-and-patch group across 1 directory with 22 updates

question: Should maintainers accept this 22-package production dependency bump as one grouped update, or split higher-risk runtime packages before merge?
rationale: The patch is mechanically clean and CI is green, but automation cannot fully decide whether the grouped compatibility and rollback risk is acceptable for ClawHub production dependencies.

options.title: Accept Grouped Bump
options.body: Merge the PR as a single maintenance update after maintainer review of the green checks, preview, and dependency scope.

options.title: Split Higher-Risk Packages
options.body: Ask for Convex/TanStack/Sharp or other runtime-sensitive packages to be separated into smaller PRs with narrower rollback units.

options.title: Pause Until Regression Evidence
options.body: Leave the PR open until a maintainer or user-visible smoke path identifies whether any package-specific risk needs action.

recommendation.title: Accept Grouped Bump
recommendation.body: Merge the PR as a single maintenance update after maintainer review of the green checks, preview, and dependency scope.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent package and release work on the same manifests makes this the best available routing candidate for the merge-risk choice.
